Chapter Ten: The Invitation to Repaint—Living a Faith That Grows
So, picture this—faith isn’t some finished masterpiece that gets hung up on the wall, admired from a distance, and left untouched. No, it’s more like a work in progress, a canvas that’s always being repainted, a story that’s still unfolding with each new chapter.
The real invitation? It’s not about defending the old picture. It’s about picking up a brush and joining in, helping to create something new and alive.
Now, imagine a group of friends gathered around a dinner table, laughter and stories bouncing from wall to wall. One person shares how their faith has shifted over time. Someone else talks about a new spiritual practice they’ve tried. Another just honestly says, “Hey, I’m still figuring things out.”
There’s no pressure to agree, no need to act like you’ve got everything together. The room is just full of color, of life, of possibility.
You know, most people don’t realize how much freedom there is in letting go of the need to have every answer. The journey of faith isn’t about reaching a final destination. It’s about walking together, staying open to change, to growth, to being surprised along the way.
The invitation is to live with open hands, open hearts, and open minds—to trust that God is always at work, always inviting, always creating something new.
There’s this story about someone who, after years of trying to fit in, finally found the courage to just be themselves. They stopped pretending, stopped hiding, stopped chasing perfection. And let me tell you, the relief was overwhelming—the freedom was real.
In that moment, faith stopped being about rules, and started being about relationship. It became less about having all the answers, and more about love.
So here’s the thing—the journey keeps going, the story isn’t finished.
The invitation is to keep repainting your canvas, to keep asking questions, to keep seeking, and to trust that, yes, the best is still ahead.
